comment: Sampling plan for the ML-Pulay dataset. Each group is a family of systems
and the CP2K settings that suit it. The point of grouping is diversity: a
dataset drawn from one family teaches a mixer that family's B and nothing
else, which is how the first trained model failed to transfer.
Groups are cheap-to-expensive top to bottom; a run can stop early and
still produce a valid, if narrower, dataset.

groups.name: small_molecules
groups.description: Closed-shell molecules, equilibrium and strained. Small n_ao, short SCF, cheap.

groups.name: periodic_main_group
groups.description: Semiconductors and ionic solids. Periodic boundary conditions change the g-space residual, and therefore B.

groups.name: transition_metal_oxides
groups.description: Open d shells: the slowest-converging systems here, and the ones a mixer is actually wanted for. Smeared occupations and empty states.
